$comment: Immutable Core Hub token contract. A subsystem MUST validate every field listed here.
jwksFormat: RFC 7517 - the response body MUST be {"keys":[...]} with no wrapper

refreshTokenAudience.$comment: Planned with Core Hub's token-scope work: refresh tokens get their own audience, so the aud check of every subsystem rejects them. Subsystems never receive refresh tokens.

sso.$comment: Central SSO, standards 1.1 (auth-contract.md section 5). Every sign-in starts at the subsystem's login path; the browser is sent to Core Hub's WEB app, never to the API's ssoAuthorizePath, which needs a Bearer header a redirect cannot carry.

claims.sub: Core Hub user id - the only identity a subsystem may trust. Opaque string up to 64 characters, NOT always a UUID (CSV-imported students are user-<studentCode>); store as text, never parse or validate as UUID; personal data
claims.email: Core Hub email - display only, never a key (an MJU SSO account may be <code>@sso.mju.local and can change)
claims.role: role of the user for this subsystem: the account's core role, or the role of an approved subsystem exception (student | alumni | staff | lecturer | guest | admin); read it from every request
claims.sid: Core Hub session id - informational only; there is no endpoint to check it
claims.iat: issued at (epoch seconds) - required for the lifetime check
claims.azp: authorized party - the registered subsystem name the token was issued for. Planned: Core Hub adds it to every token it hands to a subsystem. When present it MUST equal the subsystem's own name

mustReject: unknown kid after one JWKS refresh
a token without iat, or with exp - iat greater than maxTokenLifetimeSeconds + clockToleranceSeconds (for example a refresh token)
an azp different from the subsystem's own registered name
mustIgnore: claims not listed here - Core Hub may add claims without breaking the contract

plannedChanges.next: After Core Hub's token-scope work is deployed: every token handed to a subsystem carries azp, refresh tokens use refreshTokenAudience, Core Hub refuses subsystem tokens outside the allowlisted data endpoints (reference-data.md), and approved subsystem exceptions set the role claim. A later standards release then makes azp mandatory. aud stays csmju2030 - this replaces the earlier plan to make aud the subsystem name.
plannedChanges.v2.0: The SSO handoff becomes authorization code + PKCE, so the access token no longer travels in the callback URL.
